card.name: Right before "discontinued" in warnings
card.fires_on: Small words like "be" or "should" right before an expected "discontinued" or "terminated", after an "if a reaction occurs" clause. Also the drug-name end before "should be discontinued".

modes.label: The stop-the-drug wording
modes.description: The word before "discontinued" when a reaction or event is said to call for stopping the drug or infusion.
modes.example: If an allergic reaction occurs, ampicillin and sulbactam for injection should<< be>> discontinued and the appropriate therapy instituted.

modes.label: The negated stop wording
modes.description: The word "be" after "need not" when the text says treatment does not have to be stopped.
modes.example: If a gout flare occurs during treatment, febuxostat tablets need not<< be>> discontinued.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning stop or abort, such as abort, abandon and terminate.
card.plain: It lights up when a label is about to say the drug should be stopped.
